The diff changed `return role == "admin" and tenant_id == document_tenant` to `return role == "admin" or tenant_id == document_tenant`. No callers/guards elsewhere (repo-wide grep for can_access found only the definition). Trust boundary: caller-supplied role/tenant_id now bypasses tenant isolation.

issues.description: `can_access` was changed from `and` to `or`, so it authorizes any role within the same tenant and also authorizes admins from other tenants, violating the README contract "Only administrators in the document's tenant may access it."
issues.rationale: README.md states "Only administrators in the document's tenant may access it." The diff changed `role == "admin" and tenant_id == document_tenant` to `role == "admin" or tenant_id == document_tenant` (batch.py:7). Both clauses are wrong: e.g. `can_access("viewer", "t1", "t1")` returns True (non-admin same tenant) and `can_access("admin", "t1", "t2")` returns True (cross-tenant admin). This is an authorization/trust-boundary regression.

issues.description: can_access changed from `and` to `or`, allowing non-admins in the same tenant and admins across tenants (tenant isolation breach).

The diff changed the operator to `or`, so `can_access('user','tenant-a','tenant-a')` and `can_access('admin','tenant-a','tenant-b')` both return True. This is the function that enforces the trust boundary for document access.

issues.description: `mean([])` now raises ZeroDivisionError because the empty-input guard was removed; README requires empty batches to return 0.
issues.rationale: The diff explicitly deletes `if not values: return 0` from `mean`. README.md (the repository contract) states "Empty batches must return 0." With the guard gone, `sum([])/len([])` divides by zero, breaking the documented batch-statistics contract on the empty-batch path.
issues.evidence: batch.py:3-4 reads: `def mean(values):\n    return sum(values) / len(values)`. README.md: "Empty batches must return 0. Only administrators in the document's tenant may access it." Trigger: `mean([])` -> `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`.

issues.description: `can_access` now grants access with `or`, so an admin outside the tenant OR any non-admin inside the tenant is allowed; this breaks tenant isolation.
issues.rationale: The diff changes `return role == "admin" and tenant_id == document_tenant` to `... or ...`. README.md defines the trust boundary: "Only administrators in the document's tenant may access it." The `or` grants access to (a) any admin regardless of tenant and (b) any role that matches the tenant, enabling cross-tenant admin access and unauthorized non-admin access within a tenant.
issues.evidence: batch.py:6-7 reads: `def can_access(role, tenant_id, document_tenant):\n    return role == "admin" or tenant_id == document_tenant`. Triggers: `can_access("admin", "t1", "t2")` -> True (cross-tenant admin), `can_access("viewer", "t1", "t1")` -> True (non-admin same tenant). README.md: "Only administrators in the document's tenant may access it."
